chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to me. He said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has three hallowed things that cannot be compared to anything: His Book, which is His wisdom and His light; His House, which He made the qibla for mankind - He does not accept from anyone turning toward other than it; and the progeny of your Prophet (may God bless him and his family).

key_terms.بيته: His House - the Ka'ba in Mecca, the direction of prayer (qibla)
key_terms.حرمات: Hurumat - hallowed/sacred things, sanctities that must be respected and not violated
key_terms.عترة: 'Itra - the progeny/household of the Prophet, a key concept in Shia Islam
key_terms.كتابه: His Book - the Quran, described as God's wisdom (hikma) and light (nur)

ai.seo_question: What are the three most sacred things according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) identifies three uniquely sacred things in God's creation that have no equal: the Quran (God's wisdom and light), the Ka'ba (the divinely-appointed direction of prayer from which no deviation is accepted), and the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt). This triad - Scripture, Sacred House, and Prophetic Progeny - represents the three pillars of divine guidance in Shia theology, paralleling the hadith of the Two Weighty Things (al-Thaqalayn).
